old_problem: The historical record left project-specific CPU/front-I/O path, USB-C role/orientation, fixture and acceptance values as an Engineering Decision, although the source purpose and a safe non-destructive method were already clear.
disposition_reason: ED-03, ED-07, ED-08, ED-09, ED-15 and ED-20 permit a parameterized case when the purpose, command semantics and safety boundary are known. A USB receptacle is not itself enumerable, so an approved known-good fixture supplies the detectable endpoint. Project-specific route, roles, orientations, fixture identity and thresholds remain mandatory runtime bindings, not an unresolved engineering decision.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2173, same-row DeepSeek columns, GPT V2, historical record, unique identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2174 / Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00061-V002 / a66139103d0bf627 was directly read from XLSX and its historical record.
Bind the exact CPU USB controller/root port, board header/cable/front-I/O board and USB-C receptacle before execution.
Define Type-C data/power role, required plug orientations, mux/retimer/PD path and expected negotiated mode/speed/power.
Use only an approved known-good non-storage fixture with stable descriptors and an approved bounded read-only functional query if required.
Operator performs and photographs inspection, insertion, orientation changes and removal; automation collects complete unfiltered topology/descriptors and errors.
Generic hub output, unrelated BMC/HPM scope, insecure/truncated collection, controller reset/rebind, unknown-device access and automatic retry are rejected.
No USB connection, query, physical manipulation, reset, retry or DUT action was performed.

test_case.test_name: Parameterized CPU-to-front-I/O USB-C port detection and function validation
test_case.purpose: Verify that the designated front-I/O USB-C receptacle reaches the intended CPU root port and enumerates the approved fixture in every required orientation at the approved mode without USB-C, PD, reset or overcurrent faults.
required_package: Approved fixture stable identity and safe read-only query
Operator insertion/removal procedure, thresholds, aborts and recovery
test_case.test_command: After operator route inspection and approved fixture insertion, collect complete `lsusb -t`, full descriptors for the exact fixture, Type-C/PD status where supported, negotiated speed/power and complete kernel USB reset/disconnect/overcurrent events for the bound CPU root-port chain. Repeat for every approved plug orientation; run only the approved non-destructive fixture query and then remove the fixture safely.
test_case.expected_result: For every required orientation the exact approved fixture appears only on the signed CPU-to-front-I/O route, descriptors and negotiated mode/speed/power match the oracle, the bounded function check succeeds when required, and no prohibited reset, flap, overcurrent, PD or host-health event occurs.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS only when route, fixture identity, all required orientations, descriptor/function, speed/power and signed error thresholds all match. Wrong route/identity, missing orientation, downgrade outside the oracle, failed approved query, reset/flap/overcurrent/PD or host-health breach is FAIL. Missing runtime binding or threshold is BLOCKED, never assumed PASS.
safety_gate: Gate CLOSED until route, roles, fixture, orientations, expected values, authorization and recovery are signed.
Qualified operator alone inserts, flips and removes the fixture; verify voltage/current and physical condition first.
No unknown storage/network fixture, media write, alternate-mode forcing, reset, deauthorize, rebind, log clearing or automatic retry.
Stop and safely remove the fixture on wrong route, heat, overcurrent, PD anomaly, repeated disconnect/reset or instability.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, authorization and signed project bindings
CPU root-port/header/cable/front-I/O USB-C route map and operator photos
Fixture identity and complete per-orientation topology/descriptors
Per-orientation mode/speed/power and approved read-only functional output
Pre/post USB/PD/kernel reset/disconnect/overcurrent and host-health evidence
Safe removal/restored state, discrepancy/recovery record and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Stop and preserve evidence on any anomaly. Qualified operator removes the fixture using the approved procedure and verifies the original fixture-free stable state; use only the signed recovery path and do not reset, rebind, power-cycle or retry to manufacture a pass.

source_conflict.reason: Items and Procedure consistently identify the CPU-facing front-I/O USB-C port; the generic BMC/HPM wording is only a DeepSeek defect.

blocked.reason: Purpose, safe method and recovery boundary are clear; missing route, fixture and limits are runtime project configuration.
